subject: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karen Lee <karen.lee@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback

Hi Karen —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Attached is our proposed Order Form redline (see 20270509_Lumen_OrderForm_redline.docx) that updates the term/renewal section we discussed. Two items we want to highlight for quick alignment:

1) Auto-renew cadence: We proposed a 12-month initial term with one automatic 12-month renewal unless either party gives notice. The current redline moves the customer notice window to 60 days prior to renewal. We implemented 60 days to align operationally (offboarding and data export time). Curious if LumenHealth can live with 60 vs. the 90 days procurement mentioned on call.

2) Termination for convenience (T4C): Our standard T4C includes a 60-day notice plus a pro-rated credit for pre-paid usage for the affected period. Procurement asked for a full refund for unused money; our legal is uncomfortable with that for prepaid committed capacity. The redline proposes either (A) pro-rated refund OR (B) alternative: 60-day notice + 30 days of technical transition support (to help live cutover) with no refund beyond pro-rate.

Operational asks: if Lumen insists on a 90-day notice window, we want to include a short SLA carveout that permits a quicker off-ramp for security incidents and a transitional credit schedule (we'll propose specifics).

I’ve CC’d Vivek (commercial), Marissa (legal), and Aditya (acct exec) to keep everyone looped. Please let us know if procurement/legal would prefer tracked changes in the Google doc instead of the attached Word.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270509_Lumen_OrderForm_redline.docx (Order Form redline, docx)

From: Karen Lee <karen.lee@lumenhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lumenhealth.com>, LumenHealth Legal <legal@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending. We reviewed the redline and had quick internal alignment: procurement is pushing for a 90-day notice window on auto-renew. Historically our vendor offboarding needs ~60 days, but our procurement committee has standardized on 90 to allow approvals and budget cadence.

On T4C: legal is not comfortable with pro-rated-only refunds when significant prepayments are involved. Their ask is a negotiated refund ladder: 100% refund if termination within first 30 days of term start; 50% refund if within first 90 days; thereafter pro-rata. They flagged that our audit/compliance teams require a clean financial unwind where feasible.

We can be flexible on carveouts (security incident exception is fine). If Redwood can commit to a 90-day notice but accept the refund ladder above (and maintain a 30-day transition support), procurement could sign off faster.

Would you and your legal take a pass on that ladder? If yes, we can route with legal and procurement and aim for an executive counter-sign next week.

Best,
Karen Lee
Procurement Manager
LumenHealth

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback

Looping internal thread —

Quick thoughts from a commercial perspective: 90 days is not a deal-killer from a go-to-market standpoint if we protect the following:
- We limit refund exposure to a time-boxed ladder like Karen proposed, but cap total refund amount to remaining pre-paid committed fees for the affected services (no liability for 3rd-party pass-throughs or executed professional services).
- Keep a security/carveout clause that allows immediate termination for verified security incidents with standard incident response handover; in that case we don't owe refunds beyond unused pre-paid usage.
- Add an operational breakglass to support rapid migration (30 days dedicated transition runbook + one week priority support).

Marissa — can you confirm whether the ladder Karen proposed is acceptable from a legal risk perspective if we add the refund cap language above and a narrow carveout for third-party costs? If legal prefers not to do any refunds beyond pro-rata, propose alternate commercial mitigant (e.g., credit toward future services or extended support).

Aditya — FYI on negotiation posture. If we accept the ladder, snapshot the ARR and commit levels so legal can compute max exposure.

Vivek
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback

Thanks Vivek. Reviewing Karen’s ladder, we can make that work with the following edits (high-level):

1) Refund ladder: acceptable if we: (a) explicitly limit refunds to amounts actually prepaid to Redwood for Software/Service fees (exclude pass-throughs and PS consumed), and (b) require Lumen to certify unused services via a short affidavit to reduce dispute risk.

2) Cap: we should include a monetary cap tied to the remaining committed fees for the then-current term (we can calculate this when final order form numbers are known).

3) Transition support: add 30 days of included migration support; any additional support is billable at standard PS rates.

4) Security carveout: allow immediate termination for verified critical security incidents; in that instance refunds limited to unused prepaid software fees (no extended credits).

5) Notice window: we'll accept 90-day renewal notice for the customer but request a reciprocal 60-day Redwood opt-out for convenience if capacity or regulatory constraints require us to deprecate a particular deployment region — this is a narrow operational protection, not a general escape.

Draft language snippets below for legal to paste into the Order Form (we'll provide tracked changes):
- "Termination for Convenience Refund Ladder: If Customer exercises termination for convenience within the first thirty (30) days of a Term, Customer shall be entitled to a refund of 100% of any prepaid, unused software fees; if exercised after thirty (30) days but within ninety (90) days, Customer shall be entitled to a refund of 50% of any prepaid, unused software fees; thereafter, refunds will be calculated pro rata for the remaining Term."
- "Refunds shall be limited to fees prepaid to Redwood for Software/Service; excluding third-party pass-throughs and consumed Professional Services. Customer shall provide reasonable certification of unused services to facilitate refund processing."
- "Security Incident: Either party may terminate immediately in the event of a verified critical security breach affecting production confidentiality or availability; refunds in such case are limited to unused prepaid software fees."

If you want, I can prepare a clean tracked-change doc with these edits and a short playbook (eot_playbook_v1.pdf) listing operational steps for offboarding and data export windows.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: eot_playbook_v1.pdf (End-of-Term playbook, pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karen Lee <karen.lee@lumenhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: End-of-Term mechanics: LumenHealth Order Form — notice cadence & T4C fallback

Karen — appreciate the quick turnaround and the specifics. The refund ladder Marissa proposed sounds like a fair middle ground. Two quick commercial asks from Lumen’s side that we should confirm before legal routes the final:

1) Confirmation that the refund cap will be the remaining prepaid fees for the active Order Form (we will compute exact exposure once the OF numbers are finalized).
2) Agreement to include the 30-day transition support (scope in playbook) at no additional charge, plus a statement that additional migration work will be quoted.

If those two points are acceptable, Kimberly and I will get Marissa’s tracked changes into the Google doc and we can run with procurement/legal for signatures.

Quick next steps: Kimberly — can you confirm you’re ok to update the Google redline and share with Karen and Lumen legal? If Lumen wants the Word doc with tracked changes instead, let us know.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
